name: Mathematics
description: A draft sequence of core mathematics ideas with practice questions for teacher review.

resources.title: Algebra: visual preview
resources.body: Draft storyboard activity: sketch and narrate one core algebra idea; this label does not refer to a published video.

resources.title: Algebra: guided practice
resources.body: Original self-guided activity: work through a short algebra example and check each reasoning step; this is a learning prompt, not an external resource.

questions.text: Solve 3x + 5 = 20.
questions.explanation: Subtract 5 to get 3x = 15, then divide by 3.

questions.text: If y = 2x - 1, what is y when x = 4?
questions.explanation: Substitution gives y = 2(4) - 1 = 7.

questions.text: Which expression is equivalent to 4(a + 2) - 3a?
questions.explanation: Distribute 4, then combine 4a - 3a to obtain a + 8.

questions.text: The product of two consecutive integers is 56. Which pair works?
questions.explanation: The consecutive integers 7 and 8 have product 56.

questions.text: For x² - 5x + 6 = 0, which are the roots?
questions.explanation: Factor as (x - 2)(x - 3) = 0.

questions.text: Which value of x makes 2(x - 3) = 10 true?
questions.explanation: Divide both sides by 2 to get x - 3 = 5, so x = 8.

questions.text: A line has slope 3 and y-intercept −2. Which equation describes it?
questions.explanation: Slope-intercept form is y = mx + b, with m = 3 and b = −2.

questions.text: If f(x) = x² + 1, what is f(−3)?
questions.explanation: Squaring −3 gives 9, and adding 1 gives 10.

resources.title: Geometry: visual preview
resources.body: Draft storyboard activity: sketch and narrate one core geometry idea; this label does not refer to a published video.

resources.title: Geometry: guided practice
resources.body: Original self-guided activity: work through a short geometry example and check each reasoning step; this is a learning prompt, not an external resource.

questions.text: What is the sum of the interior angles of a triangle?
questions.explanation: Every Euclidean triangle has interior angles summing to 180°.

questions.text: A rectangle is 8 cm long and 3 cm wide. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Area is length times width: 8 × 3 = 24 cm².

questions.text: A right triangle has legs 6 and 8. What is the hypotenuse?
questions.explanation: By the Pythagorean theorem, c² = 6² + 8² = 100, so c = 10.

questions.text: A circle has radius 4. What is its circumference?
questions.explanation: Circumference is 2πr, which is 8π for r = 4.

questions.text: Two similar triangles have corresponding side ratio 2:5. If a smaller side is 6, what is the matching larger side?
questions.explanation: The scale factor is 5/2, so 6 × 5/2 = 15.

questions.text: What is the perimeter of a square with side length 7?
questions.explanation: A square has four equal sides, so its perimeter is 4 × 7 = 28.

questions.text: An angle supplementary to 68° measures what?
questions.explanation: Supplementary angles add to 180°, and 180 - 68 = 112.

questions.text: A prism has base area 12 cm² and height 5 cm. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Prism volume is base area times height: 12 × 5 = 60 cm³.

resources.title: Probability: visual preview
resources.body: Draft storyboard activity: sketch and narrate one core probability idea; this label does not refer to a published video.

resources.title: Probability: guided practice
resources.body: Original self-guided activity: work through a short probability example and check each reasoning step; this is a learning prompt, not an external resource.

questions.text: A fair six-sided die is rolled. What is the probability of rolling a 4?
questions.explanation: One of the six equally likely faces shows 4.

questions.text: A bag has 3 red and 2 blue counters. What is the probability of drawing blue?
questions.explanation: There are 2 blue counters among 5 counters total.

questions.text: A coin is flipped twice. What is the probability of two heads?
questions.explanation: The independent head probabilities multiply: 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4.

questions.text: A card is selected from a standard 52-card deck. What is the probability it is a heart?
questions.explanation: The deck has 13 hearts out of 52 cards, so 13/52 = 1/4.

questions.text: Events A and B are independent, with P(A)=0.4 and P(B)=0.5. What is P(A and B)?
questions.explanation: For independent events, P(A and B) = P(A)P(B) = 0.2.

questions.text: A spinner has 8 equal sections, 3 green. What is the probability it does not land on green?
questions.explanation: Five of the eight sections are not green.

questions.text: A fair die is rolled. What is the probability of an even number or a 5?
questions.explanation: The outcomes are 2, 4, 5, and 6: four of six, or 2/3.

questions.text: A box has 4 white and 6 black balls. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability both are white?
questions.explanation: The probability is (4/10)(3/9) = 12/90 = 2/15.

resources.title: Calculus: visual preview
resources.body: Draft storyboard activity: sketch and narrate one core calculus idea; this label does not refer to a published video.

resources.title: Calculus: guided practice
resources.body: Original self-guided activity: work through a short calculus example and check each reasoning step; this is a learning prompt, not an external resource.

questions.text: What is the derivative of f(x) = x²?
questions.explanation: The power rule gives d(x²)/dx = 2x.

questions.text: What is the derivative of the constant function f(x) = 7?
questions.explanation: A constant does not change as x changes, so its derivative is zero.

questions.text: If f(x) = 3x³, what is f′(x)?
questions.explanation: The power rule gives 3 × 3x² = 9x².

questions.text: What is the definite integral of 2x from 0 to 3?
questions.explanation: An antiderivative is x²; x² evaluated from 0 to 3 is 9.

questions.text: For f(x) = x² - 4x, at what x-value does its minimum occur?
questions.explanation: The derivative is 2x - 4; setting it to zero gives x = 2, the parabola’s minimum.

questions.text: What is the derivative of 5x - 3?
questions.explanation: The derivative of a linear function ax + b is its slope a.

questions.text: A position function is s(t)=t². What is the instantaneous velocity at t=4?
questions.explanation: Velocity is s′(t)=2t, so at t=4 it is 8.

questions.text: Which limit defines the derivative of f at x?
questions.explanation: The derivative is the limiting difference quotient as the input change h approaches zero.

resources.title: Statistics: visual preview
resources.body: Draft storyboard activity: sketch and narrate one core statistics idea; this label does not refer to a published video.

resources.title: Statistics: guided practice
resources.body: Original self-guided activity: work through a short statistics example and check each reasoning step; this is a learning prompt, not an external resource.

questions.text: What is the mean of 2, 4, and 6?
questions.explanation: Add the values and divide by three: 12/3 = 4.

questions.text: What is the median of 1, 3, 8, 10, 12?
questions.explanation: The middle of five ordered values is the third value, 8.

questions.text: Which measure is most resistant to a single extremely large outlier?
questions.explanation: The median depends on rank, so an extreme value usually has little effect on it.

questions.text: A data set has mean 10. If 5 is added to every observation, what is the new mean?
questions.explanation: Adding a constant to every value raises the mean by that same constant.

questions.text: A population has standard deviation 4. If every value is multiplied by 3, what is the new standard deviation?
questions.explanation: Scaling every observation by 3 scales standard deviation by |3|.

questions.text: The values are 4, 4, 5, 7. What is the mode?
questions.explanation: The mode is the most frequent value; 4 appears twice.

questions.text: If the correlation between two variables is −0.9, what does that indicate?
questions.explanation: A correlation near −1 indicates a strong negative linear association, not causation.

questions.text: A sample mean is 20 with standard error 2. Using a normal approximation, about what is a 95% confidence interval?
questions.explanation: An approximate 95% interval is mean ± 2 standard errors: 20 ± 4.

resources.title: Linear Algebra: visual preview
resources.body: Draft storyboard activity: sketch and narrate one core linear algebra idea; this label does not refer to a published video.

resources.title: Linear Algebra: guided practice
resources.body: Original self-guided activity: work through a short linear algebra example and check each reasoning step; this is a learning prompt, not an external resource.

questions.text: What is the result of [1, 2] + [3, 4]?
questions.explanation: Add corresponding components: (1+3, 2+4) = (4, 6).

questions.text: What is the dot product of [2, 1] and [3, 4]?
questions.explanation: The dot product is 2×3 + 1×4 = 10.

questions.text: What is the determinant of [[1, 2], [3, 4]]?
questions.explanation: For a 2×2 matrix, ad - bc = 1×4 - 2×3 = −2.

questions.text: Which vector solves x + y = 5 and x - y = 1?
questions.explanation: Adding equations gives 2x=6, so x=3 and y=2.

questions.text: For A=[[2,0],[0,3]], what are its eigenvalues?
questions.explanation: A diagonal matrix has its diagonal entries as eigenvalues.

questions.text: What is 3 times the vector [−1, 2]?
questions.explanation: Scalar multiplication multiplies each component by 3.

questions.text: What is the magnitude of vector [3, 4]?
questions.explanation: Magnitude is √(3²+4²) = √25 = 5.

questions.text: Two vectors are orthogonal when their dot product is what?
questions.explanation: Perpendicular vectors have zero dot product.
